subject: Archaeology
title: Atlantis: The Myth That Won't Die
description: A micro-lesson that makes Atlantis: The Myth That Won't Die usable.

hook.text: Plato described a powerful island civilization that sank beneath the sea.

buildup.text: Plato placed Atlantis beyond the Pillars of Hercules, describing a ringed city with advanced technology that angered.

discovery.text: Atlantis has been 'found' in Spain, Morocco, Antarctica, the Bahamas, Sardinia, and the eye of the Sahara.

twist.text: Plato likely invented the story as a philosophical parable about hubris and divine punishment — not a historical.

climax.text: The Thera eruption and destruction of Minoan Crete may have inspired the legend — a real civilization destroyed by.

punchline.text: A philosopher invented a moral story. The world spent 2,400 years looking for.

quiz.question: What is the most likely explanation for Plato's Atlantis story?
options: It was based on a lost Egyptian map found in Alexandria's library
It was a philosophical parable about hubris, possibly inspired by the Minoan collapse
It was a coded message describing the location of real treasure
